 When Pakistan Loses, Its Cricket Fans Disappear: Wasim Akram
 24 Oct - 30 Oct, 2026 
 Mag The Weekly 
 Fab Fun Find 
 Cricket legend Wasim Akram believes Pakistan’s declining on-field performance is affecting the younger generation’s interest in the sport. “When the team doesn’t perform well, the followers disappear,” he said in a recent interview. Akram, who never pushed his sons to follow in his cricketing footsteps, noted that children of celebrities often face immense pressure when pursuing their parents’ professions. “I never pushed them towards playing cricket. They could do whatever they wanted to do,” he said.
 Reflecting on his playing days in the 1980s and 1990s, Akram recalled a time when cricket stars were national heroes and fans gathered to welcome the team and seek autographs. “We were their heroes, Captain Imran Khan and his entire team,” he remembered.
 Despite the contrast with today, Akram said he is content with life beyond his playing career. “You can’t change the past, you can only plan the future and you have to live in the present.”
